full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chaklader J: This Rule, at the instance of defendants, directed against judgment and decree dated 10-3-2011 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka allowing Title Appeal No. 43 of 2010 there by decreeing Title Suit No. 89 of 2009 on reversing those dated 31-1-2010 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka.

2. The case of plaintiffs is that, Jahed Ali was the owner of the suit property and his name was recorded in SA khatian No. 23; Darbesh Ali and Probhat Ali were the owners of CS khatian No. 29 and Fallen was the owner of CS khatian No. 31. Jahed Ali died leaving two sons, Fazar Ali and Razzab Ali who enjoyed the suit land and their names have been recorded in SA khatian correctly having title thereto, mutated theirs names and have been paying rents regularly. Fazar Ali died leaving 5 sons and Razzab Ali died leaving 4 sons. Government acquired 0.94 acres of land out of 1.12 acres of land in CS dag No. 802, 0.21 acres of land out of 0.23 acres in CS dag No. 822, 0.78 acres of land out of 0.94 acres of land in CS dag No. 823 in LA Case No. 8/64-65. As a result in CS dag Nos. 802, 822 and 823 there is non acquired 0.40 acres of land which has been owned and possessed by the plaintiffs. They have enjoying the suit land of 0.40 acres by constructing Mosque and by paying rents after mutation having possession thereto. When they came to know of the aforesaid LA case, they applied to Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka for knowledge about position of their land. Deputy Commissioner replied that the land of plaintiffs is out of the acquired land and gazette notification was published to that effect in 2003. By order of defendant No.1 when learned Magistrate went to demolish plaintiffs' constructions, they raised objection and produced certified copy of Award Certificate. Magistrate refrained from demolishing the structures. Since the suit land has not been acquired in LA Case No. 8/64-65, plaintiffs filed the suit.

3. Defendant Nos. 1-4 contested the suit by filing written statement. We will reproduce the entire written statement later. Trial court found 0.40 acres of land has not been acquired by the Government, defendant Nos. 1-4 but dismissed the suit holding that as per section 169 of Town Improvement Act no notice having been served upon defendants as such, the suit is barred by law. In appeal, the learned Judge of the appellate court allowed the appeal finding that before filing of the suit, notice was served under section 169 of the Town Improvement Act. The notice is on record but it was not marked exhibit, learned Judge exhibited the notice as exhibit X. Learned Judge on reference to exhibit 6, found that suit land is out of acquired land, allowed the appeal and decreed the suit.

4. Mr Mahbubey Alam with Mr Md Aminul Islam, learned Advocates, appeared for the defendant-petitioners, on producing supplementary affidavit submits that, since portion of the land of the dags has been acquired by the Government, to find out whether the suit land is out side the acquired land plaintiffs ought to relay the suit land, in absence of which the suit would fail which the learned Judge did not at all consider. Learned Advocate further submits that this land having valuable land which has been acquired by Government in 1950 and gazette notification have been published acquiring entire lands of the dags but in gazette notification of 2003, it is shown portion of the dags have been acquired, which requires for a decision as to which gazette notification shall prevail but the learned Judge of the appellate court without deciding this vital question of law, decreed the suit. Learned Advocate further submits that if in this way the lands are grabbed by the local people then Government shall suffer immense loss and injury in losing valuable land.

5. Application made on behalf of Dhaka Electricity Supplier Co (DESCO) for addition of parties at this stage, is rejected.

6. Let us proceed with our judgment.

7. It is the plaintiffs' case that suit land is out side the acquired land. It has been stated in the plaint and reflected in the depositions. Let us find whether plaintiffs' such assertion has been denied in any manner by the defendants. We have seen that learned Judge took the view that defendants did not at all make out any case and it is defendant's case that 'plaintiff is to prove his case.' Here we may quote entire written statement of defendant Nos. 1-4 which is as follows:-

১ ৷ অত্র মোকদ্দমাটি দায়েরের কোন কারন নাই। কারনের অভাবে অত্র মােকদ্দমা সরাসরি খারিজ হইবে৷

২ ৷ বাদীর মোকদ্দমাটি বর্তমান আকারে ও প্রকারে চলিতে পারে না। বাদী কর্তৃক উপরোক্ত মোকদ্দমা রুশুকরন আইনের দৃষ্টিতে বিচার বিষয়ক প্রক্রিয়া অপব্যবহার নামান্তর বটে, তাই মোকদ্দমাটি সরাসরি খারিজযোগ্য৷

৩৷ বাদীর মোকদ্দমাটি সুনির্দিষ্ট প্রতিকার আইনে তিষ্টনীয় নহে৷ তাই অত্র মোকদ্দমাটি খারিজ যোগ্য৷

৪। বাদীর মোকদ্দমাটি এষ্টাপেল, একূইসেন্স ও ওয়েভার দ্বারা বারিত, তাই মোকদ্দমাটি খারিজ হইবে৷

৫। বাদীর মোকদ্দমাটি টাউন ইমপ্রুভমেন্ট এ্যাক্ট এর ১৬৯ ধারার বিধান মতে বারিত ৷ বাদী মোকদ্দমা দায়েরের ৩০ দিন পূর্বে কোন নোটিশ দেন নাই এবং মোকদ্দমাটিতে তৎপ্রেক্ষিতে কোন উল্লেখ নাই।

৬ ৷ বাদীর এই মোকদ্দমাটি পক্ষদেষে দুষ্ট তাই ইহা সরাসরি খারিজযেগ্যে ।

৭ ৷ অত্র মোকাদ্দমাটির আরজিতে বাদী পক্ষ ১নং দফায় যাহা বর্ননা করিয়াছেন তাহা রেকডীয় বিষয় যাহা প্রমাণের দায়িতু বাদী পক্ষের৷

৮। অত্র মোকদ্দমাটিৱ আরজ্যিত বাদী পক্ষ ২, ৩, ও ৪ নং দফায় যাহার বর্ননা করেছেন তাহা মালিকানা ও ওয়ারিশান সম্পর্কিত এবং রেকর্ডীয় বিষয়৷ যাহা প্ৰমানের দায়িত্ব বাদী পক্ষের৷

৯ ৷ অত্র মোকদ্দমড়াটির আরজিতে বাদী পক্ষ ৫, ৬ ও ৭ নং দফায় যাহা বর্ণনা করিয়াছেন তাহা রেকডীয় বিষয়৷ যাহা প্ৰমানের দায়িত্ব বাদী পক্ষের৷

১০৷ অত্র মোকদ্দমাটির আরজিতে বাদী পহ্ম ৮ ও ৯ নং দফায় যাহা বর্ননা করিয়াছেন তাহা দখল সংক্রান্ত ও রেকর্ডিয় বিষয়৷ যাহা প্ৰমানের দায়িত্ব বাদী পক্ষের৷

১১৷ অত্র মোকদ্দমাটির আরজিতে বাদী পক্ষ ১০ ও ১১নং দফায় উল্লেখ করিয়াছেন যে, বাদী পক্ষের নালিশী সম্পত্তি রেকর্ড ভুক্ত হয় নাই৷ বিবাদীরে নামে রেকর্ডভুক্ত হইয়াছে৷এহেন অবস্থায় বিবড়াদী পক্ষ নালিশী সম্পত্তি ঊদ্ধারের চেষ্টা করিয়া সঠিক কাজ করিয়াছেন৷

১২৷ অত্র মোকদ্দমাঢিতে আরজ্যিত বাদী পক্ষ বিবাদী পক্ষকে শুধু হয়রানি করার জন্য অত্র মামলায় জড়িত করিয়াছেন। যেহেতু অত্র মোকদ্দমায় বিবাদী পক্ষ কোন প্রকার অন্যায় বা হয়রানি মুলক কোন কাজ করে নাই বা অন্যায়ভাবে উচ্ছেদ অভিযান কাজ পরিচালনা করেন নাই ৷ সেহেতু বাদী পক্ষের উক্ত মামলা সরাসরি খারিজ হইবে এবং বাদীপক্ষ কোন প্রকার প্রতিকার পাইতে হকদার নহেন৷

১৩ ৷ বাদীর অত্র মোকদ্দমায় সৎ এবং যুক্তিপুর্ণ মামলা প্রমান করা সহ আইনে যে সকল শর্ত বিদ্যমান রাখা হইয়াছে বাদীর মোকদ্দমা বা দরখাস্তে এইরুপ কোন উপকরণ বিদ্যমান নাই।

১৪। বিবাদীগণ অত্র লিখিত জবাবে যাহা স্বীকার বা অস্বীকার করিতেছে না তাহা অস্বীকৃত বলিয়া গন্য হইবে৷

8. On a reading of this written statement we are very sorry to mention that how the learned Advocate drafted this written statement. It appears that the learned Advocate performed his duty by drafting and presenting the written statement, not discharging the legal responsibility. To draft a written statement it requires mastermind both over fact and law as in front of defendant the fact of the plaint case is open which required legally denying and defendant's fact requires to be presented probable both in law and on fact. The quoted written statement does not cover any of the requirements of Order VIII of the Code of Civil Procedure rather it demolishes defendant's case. Possession of plaintiffs has not been denied. Plaintiffs filed CS and SA khatian and also a number of rent receipts. Gazette notification dated 27-3-2003 show 0.90 acres of land was acquired out of 1.12 acres of land of CS dag No. 802, 0.21 acres of land out of 0.23 acres of land of dag No. 822 and 0.78 acres of land out of 0.94 acres of land of dag No. 823 and owners of those lands got the compensation for it. Now the plaintiffs claimed 40 decimals of land from aforesaid three dags which have not been acquired. On this question it is concurrent finding of fact which has been arrived on reference to the deposition and exhibits is immune from interference.

9. On the question of service of notice, appellate court found notice was served an the notice has been filed and is in record, which has been marked as exhibit X, as such, the ground upon which the suit was dismissed by the learned Assistant Judge was legally set aside.

10. On the question of two gazette notification, one of 1950 and other of 2003, which one is to be prevailed. Mr Mahbubey Alam, learned Advocate produce gazette notification of 1950, wherein all the dags of the suit in its entirety have been acquired submits that the gazette notification of 1950 if given effect then the suit would be dismissed. It is to be noted that after 1950, in 1965 there is gazette notification over the lands of the suit and in continuation, Gazette notification of 2003 published partly acquiring the lands, leaving 40 decimals out of acquired land. Government did not say anything as regard to any of the gazette notification in written statement. Over the selfsame property if there be two or three gazette notifications, like the suit in our hand, unless Government could produce any paper or document or make out any case, then the latest gazette notification is to be taken as the gazette notification for the lands mentioned therein. Mr Mahbubey Alam, learned Advocate, now before this Court canvassing for gazette notification of 1950 but no foundation to consider this Gazette notification has been made in the written statement as such it cannot be accepted.

11. Written statement shows the ignorance of the learned Advocate who drafted it. Unless the averments of the plaint be denied then it is taken to be admitted by the defendant. We have already quoted the entire written statement and on a reading of the same we are very sorry to mention that this kind of written statement cannot be said to be a written statement for defending the defence case. Even in this written statement the 'actual fact' has not been mentioned. Here we may refer to the decision of Nurul Islam vs Jamila Khatun, 53 DLR (AD) 45, wherein it is held "in view of the said facts since this specific assertion was not denied specifically by the defendants either in their written statements or in evidence nor any issue was framed or the contesting defendants raised the same before the trial Court we are not inclined to permit the defendants to raise such a question before this court." On consideration of the materials on record we find nothing to disagree with the said finding of the High Court Division." In the case of Dr. Jagjit Singh vs Giani Kartar Singh, AIR 1966 SC 773 and in the case of Zahuri Sah vs Dwarika Prasad Jhunjhunwala, AIR 1967 SC 109 similar view was taken. In the case of Narayan Chandra Saha vs Jatindra Chandra Saha, 52 DLR 5 it is held that "In view of the above provisions of law, it should be clear that right to appear and answer an appeal as given under rule 12 is completely different from that to contest a suit by filing a written statement under rule 8(8) of the Code. So the appellate Court fell in serious error of law in equating both the rights as same and in allowing the opposite parties No. 1 and 2 to file their written statement for the first time in appeal and in accepting the same for the appellate Court does not have such power. The impugned order of the appellate Court was, therefore, passed in excess of its jurisdiction and that has resulted in an error occasioning failure of justice and, as such, is liable to be set aside and is accordingly, set aside. The application of the opposite parties No. 1 and 2 dated 27-2-95 before the Appellate Court for acceptance of their written statement ought to be rejected and is accordingly, rejected."

12. In the case of Maran Mondal vs Additional Deputy Commissioner, 6 BLT 22 it is held that "Order VII, rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides that assertion of facts made in the plaint if not denied specifically or by necessary implication, shall be deemed to be admitted. In our case under review the plaintiff clearly stated in the plaint that Lakshman Mondal had died in this country as a citizen of the erstwhile East Pakistan leaving the plaintiff as his only heir to succeed him and he led evidence to prove the said assertion by the unchallenged oral and documentary evidence and there being no contrary evidence on record, the learned Courts below clearly erred in law in dismissing the suit ignoring the positive evidence on record by resorting to hypothetical assumptions and the same has resulted in error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice."

13. In the case of Syed Ali Sarder (Parary) vs Shahabuddin Ahmed Chowdhury, 18 DLR 198 it is held that "Where a plaintiff makes claim to the case land, the defendants being in possession resists that claim, he must resist it upon all the grounds known to him. I find support for this view in the case of Srimut Rajah Mootoo Vijaya Raganadha Bodha Gooroo Sawmy Peria Odaya Taver vs Katama Natchair alias Coolunda poory, Zamindar of Shivagunga, and Armonga Taver Moor's (4), the following observation appears in that case:

"When a Plaintiff claims an estate, and the Defendant, being in possession, resists that claim, he is bound to resist it upon all the grounds that it is possible for him, according to his knowledge, then to bring forward."

14. In the case of Shamsul Haque vs Sarafat Ali, 46 DLR 57 it is held that "The learned Advocate for the petitioner assailed the judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court on several grounds. He submits first, that the judgment of the lower appellate Court is not a proper judgment of reversal inasmuch as the lower appellate Court in reversing the finding of possession of the trial Court did not at all advert to the reasoning of the trial Court. Secondly, the lower appellate Court committed an error of law in holding that the suit is barred by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. Thirdly, it committed an error of law holding that the defendant proved his title and possession in the disputed land although the defendant did not specifically deny the allegations made by the plaintiff in the plaint under Order VIII, rule 5 CPC in the written statement. In this respect the learned Advocate cited the case of Shriram Surajmal vs Shriram Jhunwalla, 1936 Bom 285.

15. Mr Abdur Rashid also argued that the lower appellate Court committed a serious error in law in its decision in finding possession of the defendants although the defendants did not specifically deny the allegation on possession of the plaintiffs by filing written statements or pleading. Under Order VIII, rule 5 CPC the defendant is required to be specifically the allegation made in the plaint. But in the instant case the defendant did not deny the allegation of possession made by the plaintiffs in the plaint and, as such, the defendant is not entitled to lead evidence to prove his possession. But the lower appellate Court without noting this provision of law took into consideration the evidence of the defendant on possession and thereby committed an error of law in its decision. Mr Rashid, placing reliance upon Order VIII, rule 5 CPC further submits that the defendant No. 4 does not suffer from any disability. Therefore, the legal consequence of Order VIII, rule 5 CPC in absence of any denial of the allegation made in the plaint so far it relates to possession must follow. Now, let me examine the decision cited by the learned Advocate in support of the provision of law. In the case of Shriram Surajmal, Beaumont CJ observed that under Order VIII, rule 5 every allegation of fact in the plaint must be taken as admitted unless denied or stated to be not admitted in the pleading of the defendant, and where there is no pleading of the defendant, there can be non-admission on his part and he is bound by all the allegations in the plaint. Being in respectful agreement with the aforesaid view of the learned Judge I am also of the opinion that where there is no denial of the allegation made by the plaintiff in the pleading of the defendant, the defendants cannot base his case on the evidence adduced by him and the allegation of the plaintiff must be said to have been admitted by the defendant. A party cannot adduce evidence unless he pleads his case in the pleading. In this case there being no specific denial of the assertion of the plaintiffs with regard to their possession in the written statement of the defendant is bound by the allegation of the plaintiffs. In the light of this position of law the finding of possession arrived at by the lower appellate Court is also liable to be set aside. It also appears that the lower appellate Court dismissed the suit on the ground that the plaintiffs did not specifically mention the land in suit. Mr Rashid submits that this finding is the result of non-application of judicial mind on the pan of the lower appellate Court and this has occasioned failure of justice. Mr Rashid has invited my attention to the schedule to the plant. On examination of the schedule to the plaint it seems to me that the plaintiff has categorically stated the area of the suit land by describing its boundary. Thus, it also shows Mr AM Khan, the learned Additional District Judge, has not at all applied his judicial mind in deciding the appeal, more so while reversing the judgment of the trial Court. It is well settled that in a judgment of reversal the lower appellate Court should be more careful in its decision and discuss the evidence relied on by the trial Court which is not so required in a judgment of affirmance where a general agreement with the marooning of the trial Court is sufficient. The manner in which the learned Additional District Judge dealt with this appeal is deprecated." In the case of Govindasami Padayachi vs Sami Padayachi, AIR 1923 (Madras) 114 it is held that "When an allegation of fact is explicitly relied on in the plaint and there is no denial of it in the written reply of the defendant except a general one vis, that facts not admitted must be proved, the general denial will not safeguard defendant's interest unless there is something in the course of trial to justify a suspicion that the defendant was taken by surprise or there was misunderstanding. In the case of a minor defendant however there is an accepting which relates to persons under disability in Order VIII, rule 5, CPC."

<u>16. Since all the courts have opined that unless there be denial of all the averments made in the plaint in written statement specifically or by necessary implication the averments made in the plaint shall be taken to be admitted. That means, defendant at first made foundation of defence and thereafter evidence to be led. It there is no foundation of defendant's case in the written statement, defendants are not allowed to led evidence. Together with this view, exhibit-6 may be quoted as:</u>

<u>বিষয়ঃ সড়ক ও জনপথ অধিদপ্তরের অধিগ্রহনকৃত এলাকায় অধিগ্রহন আওতায় বহির্ভূত ভূমিতে নির্মান/হস্তান্তর কায্যক্রমের জন্য অনাপতি প্ৰসংগে৷</u>

<u>সূত্রঃ তত্ত্বাবধায়ক প্রকৌশলী (সওজ), ঢাকা সড়ক সার্কেল, ঢাকার স্বারক নং-২৮৬৮ ভাং-২৩-৮-২০০৩ ইং।</u>

<u>উপরোক্ত বিষয়ে জানানো যাইতেছে যে, আপনার আবেদনে উল্লিখিত ফায়দাবাদ মৌজাস্থিত সি,এস, দাগ নং-৮৩২(আংশিক), ৮২২(আংশিক) এবং আস,এস, দাগ নং-২০০১ এ বর্নিত ভূমি (নক্সা সংযুক্ত) সড়ক ও জনপথ অধিদপ্তরের অধিগ্নহনকৃতা সীমানা বহির্ভূত বিধায় সওজ বিভাগ হইতে অনাপত্তি প্রদান করা হইল৷</u>

<u>প্রকাশ থাকে যে, এই অনাপত্তি পত্র দ্বারা আবেদনকারীর স্বপক্ষে (আপনার) উল্লেখিত জমির মালিকানা বুঝাইবে না।”</u>

<u>17. We have seen from the Government papers that the portion of the land have been acquired by the Government not the land of the whole dag. It is not justifiable. If portion of land acquired then in the gazette there must be specification as to which portion of the dag has been acquired and which portion left out. We draw our attention to Government that in future when land is acquired, Government should at first measure and demarcate the land Government wanted to acquire. We here refer to some admitted factum. Here only 40 decimals of land is in dispute claimed by the plaintiffs but it is in broad day light that hundreds of acres of lands have been grabbed by the branded, marked land grabbers, in that case we always seen neither Government nor DIT took any positive step against such sin rather for the known reason they took avoiding tactics and for some obvious reason they are tight handed. We find no substance in the rule.</u>

<u>In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. Send down the lower court records. Communicate this judgment at once.</u>

End.

lawyer:
Mr. A. W. Bhuiyan, Additional Attorney-General, instructed by Mr. B. Hossain, Advocate-On-Record ------ for the Appellant. 
Dr. Rafiqur Rahamen, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr. Sharifuddin Chaklader, Advocate-On-Record ------ for the Respondent.
parties:
Bangladesh ------ Appellant
Vs.
Md. Fazlul Huq ------ Respondent
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 3.12.84 passed by the High Court Division, Comilla Bench in Civil Revision No. 58 of 1985)
full_judgment:
M.H. Rahman, J: Respondent. Md. Fazlul Huq was appointed as a clerk in the Postal Department of the Government in November, 1965. Subsequently by an order dated 3.5.1972 he was asked to act as Inspector of Post Offices, (hereinafter in brief IPO), at Netrokona Sub-Division.

2. The order dated 3.5.1972 by which the plaintiff was asked to act as IPO was "Issued in the interest of service to have immediate effect and until further orders." The order reads as follows:

"Mr. Fazlul Huq, Clerk, Divisional Office, Mymensingh, is hereby ordered to act as Inspector of Post Offices, Netrokona Sub-Dn. Mr. Saifuddin Ahmed transferred on promotion as Assistant Supt. of Post Offices, Mymensing. Mr. Fazlul Huq shall make over charge of his branch of the fore noon of 1.5.72. He is clearly given to understand that his appointment is purely temporary and may be terminated at any time without any previous notice and showing any reason."

3. By order dated 26th June, 1976 the respondent was reverted to his substantive post and was asked to join in Mymensingh Office.

4. Respondent instituted O.C. Suit No. 253 of 1976 in the Court of Munsif, Netrokona, for a declaration that the aforesaid order dated 26th June 1976, 1976 was illegal and void.

5. The appellant contested that suit asserting, inter alia, that the plaintiff was ordered to act as an IPO. Netrokona, in the vacancy caused by Mr. Saifuddin Ahmed on temporary basis, due to non availability of qualified hand; that every IPO is required to qualify through competitive examination and that the plaintiff appeared in the competitive examination, but failed.

6. The trial Court dismissed the suit. It held that no clerk could be promoted to the cadre of IPO without passing a competitive examination as provided in Rules 297/1 of Post and Telegraphs Manual Volume I.V. The trial Court considered the gradation list of Postal Officers corrected upto 1.7.1959, that showed that ten unqualified IPOs were declared to be absorbed in the cadre, but as no evidence was led how the ten IPOs were absorbed, it held that the plaintiff could not claim to be absorbed as an IPO without having the requisite qualifications.

7. On appeal the plaintiffs prayer for declaring the order of transfer as had was rejected, but his other prayer with regard to the reversion to his post of clerk was allowed. After considering Rule 50 of the Posts and Telegraphs Manual, volume IV, which provides that vacancies from non-gazetted officers of more than one month but no more than four month duration can be filled up temporarily, and Rule 59 which provides that an IPO should not ordinarily remain in charge of the same division or at the same post for more than four years at a time, the appellate Court observed that the plaintiff held the post of IPO for more than four years and he was under the impression that he would be ultimately absorbed in the cadre of IPO. As the impugned order was passed without any notice the appellate Court after relying on Anwarul Huq Khan Vs. Government of Bangladesh and others and the Government of Bangladesh VS. Md. Ismail Hossain, 31 DLR (AD) 127 declared that the order of reversion amounted to reduction in rank and it was void and illegal. The High Court Division upheld the order of the appellate Court.

8. In 31 DLR 21 it was held that an incumbent holding a post for considerable long time is entitled to protection under Article 135 of the Constitution.

9. In the Government of Bangladesh Vs. Md. Ismail Hossain reported in 31 DLR(AD) 127 the respondent holding substantively the post of District Kanogo, was "appointed temporarily to the East Pakistan Civil Service (Executive) Class II", a temporary cadre dependent on early sanction. After seven years of service in that cadre he was reverted to his substantive post of District Kanongo without any notice. It was held that as the respondent was not appointed for a limited period within the tenure of cadre if self or any specified period and that as the word "temporarily" used in the order of appointment would mean the cadre itself and not related to the appointment, his reversion to his substantive post was treated as a reduction in rank. With this reasoning the court distinguished the ratio in Hartwell Prescott Singh Vs. The Uttar Pradesh Government and others, AIR 1953 (SC) 886, Parshotam Lal Dhingra Vs. Union of India, PLD 1958 S.C. (India) 217, Abdul Majid Sheikh Vs. Mushaffe Ahmed and another, 17DLR 1965 (SC)63, and Chairman Railway Board Vs. Abdul Majid 18 DLR (SC).

10. In the case reported in AIR 1957 (SC) 886 it was held "Reversion from a temporary post held by a person does not per se amount to reduction in rank, because, the temporary post held by him is not his substantive rank."

11. In the case reported in PLD 1958 (SC) India 217, the Indian Supreme Court held" [If] the servant has no right to the post, as when he is appointed to a post, permanent or temporary either on probation or on an officiating basis and whose temporary service has not ripended into a quasi-permanent service as defined in the Temporary Service Rules, the termination of his employment does not deprive him of any right and cannot, therefore, by itself be a punishment. One test for determining whether the termination of the service of a Government servant is by way of punishment is to ascertain whether the servant, but for such termination, had the right to hold the post. If he had a righ to the post as in the three cases herein before mentioned, the termination of his service will by itself be a punishment and he will be entitled to the protection of Art. 311. To put it in another way, if the Government has, by contract express or implied, or under the rules the right to termination in the manner provided by the contract or the rules is prima facie an per se, not a punishment and does not attract the provisions of Art. 311."

12. In State of Bombay Vs. F. A. Abraham 7 AIR 1962 (SC) 794, the India Supreme Court held that "a person officiating in a post has no right to hold it for all times. He may have been given the officiating post because the permanent incumbent was not available, having gone on leave or being away for some other reasons. When the permanent imcumbent comes back, the person officiating is naturally reverted to his original post. This is no reduction in rank, for it was the very term on which he had been given the officiating post. Again, sometimes a person is given a officiating post to test his suitability to be made permanent in it later. Here again, it is an implied term of the officiating appointment that if he is found unsuitable, he would have to go back. If, therefore, the appropriate authorities find him unsuitable for the higher rank and then revert him back to his original lower rank, the action taken is in accordance with the terms on which the officiating post had been given. It is in no way a punishment and is not, therefore. a reduction in rank."

13. The Pakistan Supreme Court consistently held in a number of decisions that revision of an incumbent to his substantive post from the higher post to which he was temporarily promoted is not a reduction in rank. Pakistan Vs. Fazal Rahman Khandkar and another PLD 1959 (SC) 82. Province of West Pakistan Vs. Bashir Ahmed. PLD 1959 (SC) 93 and Pakistan and another Vs. Qazi Syed Hikmat Hussain, PLD 1959 (SC) 107.

14. In the case reported in 18 DLR 1966 (SC) 532. Chairman, East Pakistan Railway Board, Chittagong and another Vs. Abdul Majid Sardar, Ticket Collector, P.E. Railway, the Pakistian Supreme Cowl upheld the reversion of the respondent to his substantive post of Tally Clerk from that of a Ticket Collector to which he was temporarily promoted.

15. The respondent however relied on 17 DLR (SC) 63 and 22 DLR (SC) 331 and submitted that his case is not a case of reversion simpliciter.

16. In Khushi Muhammad & others Vs. General Manager (Now Vice-Chairman), Pakistan Western Railway 22 DLR (SC) 331, as no rule was shown to the Court that an incumbent holding post in the grade in a temporary or officiating capacity should rank lower in point of seniority to one who was appointed later in the service in the same capacity against a reserved post in the same category, it was held that all the incumbents were to be treated at par in the mater of seniority in the grade after they entered it. This case has no relevancy in the case.

17. For the meaning of the term "until further order" our attention has been drawn to the following observation of Cornelius, C.J. in Abdul Majid Vs. Mushafe Ahmed, Section Officer, Govt. of Pakistan and others, 17 DLR (SC), 63 (68)." It is clearly impossible to construe the expression until further orders as conferring absolute power of retention or dismissal upon the competent authority. The matter of public employment is governed by a complex of laws, commencing with constitutional instruments and ending with statutory rules, which have been authoritatively construed, by the Superior Courts, in relevant respects. Therefore, these words can only mean that the appointee was subject to lawful orders made by competent authority."

18. Our attention is also drawn to the following observation of Kaikaues J. made in 17 DLR (SC) 63 (74):

"To repeat, the Government could not as an ordinary and permanent arrangement fill up permanent posts by employees subject to condition of termination of employment by notice. The Government could fill up the post in this manner if the Government was unable to get a person with proper qualifications and concievably in some other special circumstances, for some time, but it cannot adopt it as a rule that the post will be filled in this manner. When I ask myself the question as to why the Government is filling a permanent post in this manner, I find no answer except that the Government wants to retain a power of arbitrary termination of service so as to defeat the constitutional guarantee. No condition of service that is intended to defeat at constitutional guarantee can be permitted to be operative."

19. In this case, we find no reason to ascribe any bad motive to the appointing authority.

20. The above observations of Cornelius, C.J and Kaikaus. J, made in case of termination of service with fourteen days notice are hardly relevant in this case where there is no question of termination of service.

21. The only question calls for determination in this case is, whether the impugned reversion to the respondent's substantive post after his acting in a higher post can be termed as reduction in rank.

22. The case reported in 31 DLR (AD) 127, relied on by the appellate Court as well as by the High Court Division, came up for consideration in Saleh Ahmed Joardar Vs. People's Republic of Bangladesh 36 DLR (AD) 26. After finding that the case of Saleh Ahmed and that of Ismail Hossain of 31 DLR (AD) 127. being both case of reversion to substantive post, "substantially the same". Fazle Munim, C. J. in delivering the majority opinion held "Yet, a different conclusion must be reached by us in the case at hand" attaches to the appointment, but the temporary nature of appointment may be whittled down by any subsequent event or development. For example if an officer is appointed temporarily from one service to another service and continues in the latter service for a very long period, it may become difficult to hold that he was still a temporary officer in the latter service. On the other hand, if after such appointment he is reverted back to his parent service soon, therefore it would be equally difficult to hold that this could not be done as the expression 'temporarily' did not mean that the appointment was temporary."

23. In distinguishing the cause of Saleh Ahmed from that of Ismail Hossain, Fazle Munim C. J. observed at para 18 of the report:

"Apart from any possible change of meaning of the expression "temporarily" that may occur due to different intentions of the appointing authority or its subsequent conduct or development showing the temporary nature of the appointment, it may be mentioned that the basis upon which Court arrived at conclusion in the case of Bangladesh Vs. Md. Ismail Hossain does no longer exist in the instant case as the cadre itself in which the appellant was appointed temporarily now stands abolished. In such background, Ismail Hossain's case cannot cover the instant ease. In Ismail Hossain's case though the respondent was appointed temporarily, as the cadre itself continued to exist the appointment though temporary was held to be permanent. Had it been otherwise, that is, if the cadre stood ablished at the date of the judgment the decision of the Court would have, in all probability, been different. If the implications of Ismail Hossain's case are remembered, that is to say, if the cadre as is temporary the appointment would also be temporary but not so if the cadre itself renders that decision inapplicable to the case before us. We are told than the service was abolished in 1977."

24. Shahabuddin Ahmed. J. as he was then, in his dissent however observed in para 26 "that the East Pakistan Civil Service and in which both this appellant and Md. Ismail Hossain were "temporarily" appointed was never abolished at any time but this cadre was in existence both in 1967 when this appellant was reverted and also in 1973 when Ismail Hossain was reverted."

25. We have quoted at length some observations made in Saleh Ahmed's case as both the appellant and the respondent relied on them adding their own emphasis, but they will be of little help in the facts of this case. This instant case is not a case of abolition of cadre. Again, there is nothing in the conduct of the appointing authority to show that the respondent's temporary appointment to the post of IPO was intended to be permanent.

26. In the first few months after liberation of the country there was a shortage of qualified hands. Where strict adherence to Rule 50 as to transfer for filling temporary vacancy was not practicable the sanctioning authority under that very rule is authorised to make acting arrangement according to administrative requirements. In the departmental instructions it has been emphasised that such temporary appointment to the post of IPOs when qualified officials are not available, will not give a claim for permanent appointment or for relaxtion of conditions of recruitment to tier Inspector's cadre.

27. The post of an IPO is a promotion  post D.W. 1 asserted that there could not be any promotion to the post of IPO without appearing successfully in the competitive examination of the department. The respondent deposing as P.W. 1, conceded that he did not know any instance of promotion without passing the competitive examination. He appeared in the competitive examination of the Department during the period when he was officiating as an IPO but failed to pass that examination.

28. Our attention is drawn to Mominul Huq Vs. Bangladesh 38 D.L.R 391, where one of us, Mustafa Kamal, J. observed that where in the rules of service promotion is an act of violation, a matter of positive action to be taken by the appropriate authority, one cannot import a legal fiction. The learned Munsif in a very straigth forward manner, held that the plaintiff cannot be retained in the post for which he is not qualified, with the help of the Court.

29. Any order of reversion after an incumbent's appointment to a higher post and continuing there for some duration will surely cause a disappointment as he would no longer draw the benefits of that higher post, but that cannot be called a reduction In rank per se.

<u>30. The uninterrupted service rendered by the respondent for about five years, if considered as "one non-temporary or quasi-permanent", as suggested by the learned counsel for the respondent, even then the impugned order of reversion cannot be termed as an instance of reduction in rank for attracting the protection under Art 135 of the Constitution. The language of the impugned order indicates in unmistaken manner that it was never meant to be an order of promotion. In the facts of the case the respondent was not entitled to any show cause notice nor there was any violation of any principle of natural justice.</u>

31. Therefore, the respondent's contention that he acquired a vested right to the post of IPO by virtue of his acting in that capacity for about five years and enjoying all the emoluments and other benefits, must fail. The appeal is allowed. The judgment and decree of the trial Court are restored. No costs.

32. Before we part with the case, we like to point out and disapprove the manner in which the paper book was prepared by the appellant. Permission was sought and given to the appellant to prepare the paper book out of Court. The paper book is prepared in most clumsy manner. Not only papers of different sizes, and photocopies, not easily readable, were used, the orders mentioned in the judgments of the Courts below were not included. The very impugned order of reversion is not there. Subsequently, additional paper book has been filed containing a number of departmental circulars without mentioning whether those were exhibited or not in the trial Court. The Attorney General's Office, which looks after the litigations of the Republic, the single biggest litigant in the country, in the Supreme Court is expected to follow the rules as to preparation of paper book meticulously so that it set up a model other litigants may emulate. Prayer for dispensation of paper book or preparation of paper book out of court, if facilely prayed for and readily allowed then it would not only whittle down the rules framed for the convenience of both the Court and the counsel, it will cause further trouble if at the hearing of the appeal additional supplemental paper books are filed as an afterthought. The main object of the rules for preparation of paper book is to avoid a clutter which cannot he used as a sorting device for ascertaining facts at the last Court of the country.

End.

lawyer:
M Shafique Ahmed, Senior Advocate with Mahbub Shafique and Mr Tushar Kanti Roy, Advocates ------ For the Petitioner. 
Mohammad Idrisur Rahman with Md Shahidullah, Md Bodiuzzaman, Advocates ------ For the Contemner Nos. 1-6.
parties:
Anisul Fatemna ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Dr Khonddoker Showkat Hossain Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Public Works and others ------ Respondents-Contemners.
full_judgment:
Md Ashfaqul Islam J: At the instance of the petitioner Mrs Anisul Fatema, this Rule was issued calling upon the respondents-contemners to show cause as to why a proceeding for contempt of Court should not be drawn up against them for non-compliance with the judgment and order dated 22-4-2007 passed by this Division in Writ Petition No. 5657 of 2003 (Annexure-A) and why they will not be punished for committing contempt of Court.

2. The facts relevant for disposal of the rule, in short are that the petitioner herein filed Writ Petition No. 5657 of 2003 before this Division under Article 102 of the Constitution against the Respondent Nos. 1-3 relating to a premises measuring an area of 11 katha 6 chattak land with structures and fixtures thereon situated at Plot No. CWS (B)-84, Holding No. 18, Road No. 23, Gulshan residential area, Dhaka on the ground of enlistment of the said property in the "KA" list of Abandoned Buildings published in the Official Gazette of the Government on 23-9-1986. Upon hearing on 22-4-2007 the Rule was made absolute by this Division in the following manner-

"In the result, the rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. It is hereby declared that the inclusion of house, situated at plot no. CWS (B)-84, holding No. 18, Road No. 23, Gulshan residential area under Police Station Gulshan, Dhaka, in the 'Ka' list of the Abandoned Buildings published in Bangladesh Gazette dated 23-9-1986 under serial No. 22, Gulshan residential area at page 9762 under the provision of Abandoned Building (Supplementary Provision) Ordinance, 1985 (Act LIV of 1985) was made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. The respondents are directed to exclude the same from the said list of "Abandoned Buildings".

3. Be it mentioned that before the Writ Petition was filed the petitioner filed an application before the Court of Settlement, Dhaka for exclusion of the property from the said list but the Court of Settlement refused to accept the application by assigning reason that the same being barred by limitation and accordingly the Writ Petition No. 5657 of 2003 was filed. However, the respondent Government thereafter filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2351 of 2008 before the Hon'ble Appellate Division challenging the aforesaid judgment and order dated 22-4-2007 passed in Writ Petition No. 5657 of 2003 which was dismissed by the Appellate Division as barred by limitation and, as such, the judgment and order of the High Court Division was upheld.

4. The petitioner then sent a letter addressed to Respondent Nos.1-3 requesting them to comply with the said judgment and order dated 22-4-2007 and thereby urging exclusion of the said property from the list. The respondents duly received the said letters dated 25-11-2009 but they did not exclude the property from the list of abandoned property. Under the circumstances the petitioner finding no other way invoked jurisdiction of this Division under Article 108 of the Constitution upon which this Division issued contempt Rule upon the respondents passed on 13-2-2011.

5. Be it mentioned that time to time with the changes of the respondents new respondent-contemners have been added as added respondent-contemners and accordingly cause title of the contempt petition was modified.

6. Mr M Shafique Ahmed, the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the contempt-petitioner after placing the petition and series of supplementary affidavits mainly submits that the contemners are under a legal obligation to implement the order of the High Court Division passed in Writ Petition No. 2351 of 2003 and they cannot immune from implementing the order of this Division but sitting over it. This attitude, as he submits is defiance and willful and deliberate disregard to the order of this Court which clearly tantamounts to contemptuous disrespect to the order of this Court.

7. Further he submits that Article 112 of the Constitution mandates all public functionaries, executive and judicial, to act in aid of the Supreme Court. If the executive officials are allowed to defy the order of the Court, not only the remedy under 102 of the Constitution will be meaningless, the people will also lose confidence in the efficacy of the administration of justice causing harm to the society in general and to the rule of law in particular.

8. Mr Ahmed has also drawn our attention to the facts filing supplementary affidavit on behalf of the petitioner dated 30-11-2014 and submits that instead of implementing the decision of this Division the Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Public Works respondent No. 1 has filed a Title Suit No. 717 of 2014 before the District Judge, First Court, Dhaka for declaration of title and the judgment passed in Writ Petition No. 5657 of 2003 dated 22-4-2007 to be illegal, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiff and on 25-9-2014 respondent No. 2 appeared in the said suit and filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint and also filed written statement and the suit is pending for hearing. Therefore, the learned Senior Advocate submits that this is a further contempt of Court on the part of the contemners which shows that they are deliberately and willfully violating the clear order of this Division passed in Writ Petition No. 5657 of 2003. On that score the respondents-contemners should be punished for committing contempt of this Court.

9. Mr Mohammad Idrisur Rahman, the learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent-contemner Nos. 1-7 opposes the Rule. He filed affidavit of fact in compliance on behalf of the contemner Md Moinuddin Abdullah stating the following:-

"In compliance of the order of this court the respondent contemner personally appeared before this court on 6-5-2014. The respondent-contemner is ready to comply with the Courts order by exclusion of the house in question after being satisfied about identity of the petitioner Mrs. Anisul Fatema wife of Mr Mohibul Hoque Fakhruddin and, as such, prayed for a direction but till date the petitioner did not appear. It has been stated that in clause 26 of the lease Agreement it has been provided that when any change in ownership or possession occurs by succession or transfer, the person becoming entitled to such succession or transfer, as also the person who effect the transfer shall within one calendar month from the date thereof, give notice in writing to the Lessor of such succession or transfer provided that where one of them has given the Lessor such notice nothing in this lease shall require the other party also to give notice.

10. It has been provided under Article 6 of the Bangladesh Abandoned Property (Control, Management and Disposal) Order President Order 16 of 1972 that—

"No person shall except in accordance with the provisions of this order or any rules made thereunder transfer any Abandoned Property in any manner or create any charge or encumbrance on such property and any transfer made or charge or encumbrance created in contravention of this order shall be null and void."

11. His submissions on the basis of the said facts are that in order to comply with the order of this Division in Writ Petition No. 5627 of 2003 various steps have been taken on different occasions for ensuring the presence of the petitioner for hearing and verify her identity. It would evident from the letters dated 21-11-2012 and 22-1-2014 (Annexure-X and X-1) issued by the respondents that the petitioner was asked to appear personally before the Ministry for hearing and identification but she did not appear. It has been also stated and submitted by the learned counsel that the contemner-respondent is ready to comply with the direction of this Division and would exclude the house in question to the writ petitioner Mrs. Anisul Fatema, wife of Mohibul Haque Fakhruddin and accordingly sought for direction of this Division in this regard.

12. The liability of committing contempt of Court is absolutely individual liability i.e. the liability is upon the person who has committed the Contempt of Court. For that reason all the respondents who were in charge of the post of the Ministry time to time are relevant for the purpose of deciding who should be held liable for committing the offence as alleged. At present Mr Mohammad Moinuddin Abdullah is in charge of Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Public Works. He has entered into the office in the year 2014. The steps those have been taken by the contemner as we have seen from the materials on record, supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioner as well as the affidavit of facts in compliance filed by the contemner-respondents are not relevant for the disposal of the instant contempt petition and we do not want to embark upon those aspects since there is a case pending before the trial court upon a particular issue.

13. Let us now consider whether the mandamus given by this Division in Writ Petition No. 5657 of 2003 have been implemented and if not whether that has been done wilfully or deliberately. It indeed baffles us when we see that the contemners after the decision of the High Court Division in the year 2007 unsuccessfully went to the Appellate Division in the year 2009 and even thereafter could not implement the decision of this Division. It should have been implemented in terms of the direction of the High Court Division much earlier.

14. In the Constitutional Law of Bangladesh written by the Senior Advocate Mr. Mahmudul Islam it has been noted:—

"There is no mode of enforcing a writ of mandamus and committal for contempt of Court is the way of executing any direction given by the court in writ jurisdiction. Disobedience to the order of the court or breach of the undertaking given to the court is contempt of court. If an order passed by a competent court is clear and unambiguous and not capable of more than one interpretation, disobedience or breach of such order would amount to contempt of court. Disobedience to or failure to obey an interim order also constitutes contempt of court. There can be no laxity in such a situation because otherwise the court orders would become the subject of mockery."

15. Here we want to pin point that this Division while dealing with the contempt of Court passed necessary and consequential direction for enforcement of the directive of the order passed in original writ petition. The decision of Farook Hossain vs Iqbal Hossain reported in 8 BLC 204 is an authority on the point.

16. Moreover, our Appellate Division also came down heavily on this issue in the case of AFM Mostafa, Director General Bangladesh Railway vs Monoranjan Mojumder reported in 13 BLT (AD) 198 = 9 BLC (AD) 207. Wherein their Lordships of the Appellate Division while upholding the direction of consequential order passed by the High Court Division in Contempt Petition No. 17 of 2004 maintained:

"On consideration of the submissions advanced by the parties we are of the view that there being no mode provided for execution of the orders in writ petition the interested party may take recourse to Article 108 of the Constitution. In this view of the matter the petition filed by the respondent under Article 108 is not liable to be thrown away."

17. Notably the High Court Division in the said decision of Contempt Petition No. 17 of 2004 gave a direction for implementing the order of this Division without punishing the contemner which the Appellate Division upheld as it is.

<u>18. Admittedly we have found that the present Contemner after assuming the official charge in 2014 have taken various steps but for some reason or the other could not implement the decision of this Division. Simply because of that we cannot and should not relieve him from the charge of committing contempt of Court. But in terms of the above decision of this Division upheld by the Appellate Division we think it would be wise to direct the contemner to implement the decision of the High Court Division in terms of the decision in Writ Petition No. 5657 of 2003 instead of punishing him. The operative part of the said decision has already been quoted above. It is also recorded that the legal officer of the concerned Ministry did not properly advise the contemners to implement the judgment in its true letter and spirit leaving the petitioner to invoke remedy by way of this application under Article 108 of the Constitution.</u>

19. That being the position, the contemner-respondents are hereby directed to delist the property in question strictly in terms of the directive part of the decision in Writ Petition No. 5657 of 2003 in favour of the writ petitioner or her constituted attorney, if any, in accordance with law within 3 (three) months on receipt of this order without any fail.

20. The contemner-respondents are hereby exonerated from the liability of committing contempt of Court.

The Rule is disposed of with the direction and observations as made above.

Communicate at once.

End.

full_judgment:
SM Ziaul Karim J: This Rule, at the instance of plaintiff-petitioners, calls in question the legality and propriety of the judgment and order dated 1-7 -2004 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Second Court, Jessore in Civil Revision No. 9 of 2004, allowing the revision and reversing the order dated 5-1-2004 passed by Senior Assistant Judge, Jessore in Title Suit No. 288 of 2002, allowing the application for amendment.

2. Short facts leading to this Rule are that on 13-11-2002 petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 288 of 2002 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Jessore for declaration of title in 24 decimals of land out of 63 decimals described in the 'Schedule of the plaint.

3. The plaintiffs' case, in short, is that the suit property described in the Schedule of the plaint originally belonged to Kangali Charan Kundu under landlord Mansur Ali Sheikh, after death of Kangali Charan suit property was settled to Narendra Kumar Roy who got the patta in the name of his wife Charubala. After death of Narendra Kumar, his son Sachindra Kumar Roy Chowdhury got the suit property, but SA record prepared in the name of Charubala and one Nur Jahan but ultimately, it was corrected in his name who exchanged the suit property with Indian migrants Sheikh Ali Hossain and Sheikh Akbar Ali. Sheikh Akbar Ali and others sold the suit property to Abdul Kader Khan. The plaintiff acquired 24 decimals of land out of 63 decimals by successive kabalas from Abdul Kader Khan beginning from 20-5-1986; accordingly, records of right was prepared in their names but defendant claimed the land by virtue of a registered deed of transfer. Hence the suit.

4. The defendant-opposite party appeared in the suit by filing written statement stating, inter alia, that the suit property belonged to Munsur Ali and Kangali Charan was the tenant and after his death his successor settled the suit property to Md Ali, Bhagya Laxmi Kunda and Dulal Chandra. Thereafter, successors of landlord Munsur Ali brought Rent Suit No. 91 of 1961 in the Third Court of Munsif, Jessore for arrear of rent against them and got decree. Subsequently, in Rent Execution Case No. 245 of 1961 Mia Abul Hasan Siddique purchased the suit property in auction on 28-4-1962 and got possession on 16-1-1963 through Court: who on 27-3-2002 sold the suit land to defendant.

5. On 5-1-2004, the plaintiff filed an application for amendment of the plaint stating that some averments made in paragraph 5. will be substituted by the following statements:

প্রকৃত মালিকের অনুপস্তিতির সুযোগে তৎকালীন পূর্ব পাকিস্তান সরকার কতৃর্ক এল এ ৬৬/৬১-৬২ নং কেসে নালিশী ২২১৫ দাগের অধিগ্রহনকৃত ৩৯ শতক জমির ক্ষতিপূরণের টাকা নালিশী জমি সংক্রান্ত যত্ন সংশ্রম শূন্য যশোহর শহরের বেজপাড়া সাকিনের জনৈক আবুল কাশেম মোক্তার পিতা মৃত হুজ্জাতুল্যা যশোহর ভূমি অধিগ্রহণ কর্মকর্তার অফিসে দূনীর্তিপরায়ন কতিপয় কর্মচারীর সহিত যোগসাজস করিয়া উঠাইয়া লওয়া এক্ষনে প্রকাশ পাইতেছে । বিবাদীর জবাবে বর্ণিত মতে জনৈক আবুল হাসান সিদ্দিক নালিশী দাগের অধিগ্রহণকৃত জমির ক্ষতিপূরণের টাকা উঠাইয়া লইবার উক্তি মিথ্যা। এ সক্রান্তে কোন কাগজাদি দাখিল হইলে উহা জ্বাল, তঞ্চকী, বানোয়াট হিসাবে বিবেচিত হইবে।

And in paragraph 4 following statements will be added:

প্রতিটি ট্রাক মাটি ২৫০ টাকা হিসাবে ২৭০ ট্রাক মাটি মোট ১৭৫০০ টাকা মূল্যের মাটি দ্বারা নালিশী জমি গভীর গর্ত খাদপূর্ণ করিয়া সংস্কার করা হয়। তৎসহ ১০০০০ টাকা পারিশ্রমিক প্রদানে শ্রমিক নিয়োগ উক্ত সংস্কার করা হয়। ৩নং বাদী নালিশী জমিতে আনুমানিক ৪ ফুট পরিমান উচ্চতা পর্যন্ত ১ রুম বিশিষ্ট একটি রুম নির্মাণ কাজ সম্পন্ন করেন।

6. After hearing, learned Senior Assistant Judge by the order dated 5-1-2004 allowed the application for amendment but the same was reversed in revision by Additional District Judge, Second Court, Jessore. Hence the Rule.

7. Mr Abdul Ali, learned Advocate appearing for plaintiff-petitioners, supports the Rule and submits that learned Additional District Judge committed error of law in not considering that the proposed amendment of plaint filed by the plaintiff was necessary for the purpose of determining the real question in controversy between the parties. He adds that the proposed amendment did not introduce any new, inconsistent or contradictory material in the plaint but the same was explanatory and elucidative of facts, already asserted in the plaint. The defendant will not be in any way prejudiced by the proposed amendment. He submits that the learned Senior Assistant Judge committed no error of law in allowing the proposed amendment. In support of his contention he referred the case of Dr Abdur Rahman and others vs Bangladesh reported in 30 DLR (SC) 93, wherein it is held—

"The Court concerned shall have to find out the terms of the Rule, whether the propose amendment is likely to facilitate the determination of the real question in controversy."

8. He adds that even if the order dated 5-1-2004 is not a speaking order, it has not occasioned any failure of justice. He referred the case of Trading Corporation of Bangladesh and another vs Syed Sajeduzzaman reported in 40 DLR 406 wherein it is held—

According to the provisions of section 115, CPC, the error of law in the impugned order is not itself a ground for revision unless the said error of law has resulted in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.

9. Mr Ali lastly submits that the Court below failed to weigh and sift the materials on record as required by law and evidently fell in an error in coming to his ultimate decision occasioning failure of justice.

10. Mr Abdul Quyyum, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party, opposes the Rule without filing counter-affidavit and submits that the proposed amendment is malafide and contradictory to the effect that the plaintiff challenged the kabala by virtue of which the defendant claims the suit property but subsequently they claimed the title by it. He adds that learned Senior Assistant Judge without assigning cogent reason allowed the application for amendment. In support of his contention, he referred the case of Samela Begum vs Chandulla Mridha and another reported in 1995 BLT 130, where it is held—

"In the instant case the radical changes were sought to be introduced in the plaint by the amendment sought for and allowed by the Court. On the other hand, the learned Assistant Judge has not discussed merit of the application or of the nature and character of the amendment sought for but has passed a summary order allowing the amendment of the plaint. This is no way a judicial order. The Court did not apply its judicial mind in passing the impugned order."

11. He again referred the case of Abdul Wadud Contractor and another vs Nazir Ahmed and others reported in 48 DLR (AD) 120, wherein it is held—

"The proposed amendment introducing new facts and subsequent cause of action different from those made in the plaint if allowed condoning the delay will change the nature and character of the suit. Amendment was therefore rightly refused."

12. The learned Counsel lastly submits that the impugned order does not suffer from any illegality and calls for no interference by this Court. He however, submits that if the proposed amendment be allowed, the defendant should be given an opportunity to file additional written statement against such amendment.

13. We have gone through the plaint, written statement, application for proposed amendment, impugned order other materials on record and given our anxious considerations to the submissions advanced by the learned Counsels of both sides.

14. To appreciate the submissions advanced by the learned Counsels for both sides, let us now weigh and sift the materials on record adduced by both parties.

15. Now the question calls for our consideration, whether the Court below committed any error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned order.

16. Order VI, rule 17, Code of Civil Procedure provides that the Court may at any stage of the proceedings allow either party to alter or amend his pleading in such manner and on such terms as may be just, and all such amendments shall be made as may be necessary for the purpose of determining the real questions in controversy between the parties.

<u>17. We have considered the plaint, written statement, amendment, nature and character of the suit will not be changed and the plaintiff did not introduce any new, inconsistent or contradictory facts in the plaint. The learned Additional District Judge in his impugned order wrongly held that the plaintiff introduced some new facts by way of amendment. This view is absolutely erroneous as the amendment was explanatory and elucidative of facts already asserted in the plaint. Moreover, the plaintiff will prove his own case by adducing evidence and the defendants will be at liberty to file additional written statement against such amendment.</u>

18. In the case of A Motaleb vs Md Ershad Ali and others reported in 1998 BLD (AD) 121 = 4 BLC (AD) 150 it is held—Since all rules of the Court are intended to secure the proper administration of justice it is essential that they should be made to serve and be subordinate to that purpose so that full power of amendment may be enjoyed and, as such, it should always be liberally exercised, The only limitation in allowing an amendment of the' plaint is that the proposed amendment will not change the fundamental character and nature of the suit.

<u>19. The settled law is that amendment of pleadings may be allowed at any stage of the proceedings for the purpose of determining the real controversy between the parties.</u>

20. This view also receives support in the cases of Md Khaledur Reza Cllowdhury vs Saleha Begum and others reported in 1997 BLD (AD) 86 = 2 BLC (AD) 20, SN Roy Chowdhury vs A Jabbar and others reported in 1994 BLD 229 = 46 DLR 273, Moyezuddin Mondol vs Bena Rani Das and others reported in 45 DLR 154 and MA Jahangir and others vs Abdul Malek and others reported in 41 DLR 389.

<u>21. It is true that the learned Assistant Judge did not assign any reason in allowing the application for amendment. We find that the defendant has not in any way been prejudiced by such amendment. So, non-assigning the reason by itself is not a ground for revision unless the same has resulted in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.</u>

22. We, therefore, hold that the learned Assistant Judge rightly allowed the application for amendment and learned Additional District Judge with erroneous view reversed the same. The defendant will be at liberty to file additional written statement against such amendment.

23. We are in respectful agreement with the principle enunciated in the case reported in 1995 BLT 130 as referred by the learned Counsel for the opposite parties but the facts leading to that case are distinguishable with that of the instant case. We are therefore, unable to accept the submissions advanced by the learned Counsel for the opposite parties.

24. Having regard to the facts, the legal plea taken by learned Counsel for the petitioner prevails and appears to have a good deal of force, but we failed to discover any merit in the submissions advanced by the learned Counsel for the opposite parties.

25. In the facts and circumstances of the case and foregoing narrative, we are led to the conclusion that the impugned order dated 1-7-2004 suffers from no illegality and impropriety occasioning failure of justice. Thus, the Rule having merit succeeds. The impugned judgment and order calls for no interference by this Court.

26. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and order dated 1-7-2004 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Second Court, Jessore in Civil Revision No. 9 of 2004 is hereby set aside and the order dated 5-1-2004 passed by Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Jessore in Title Suit No. 288 of 2002 in respect of allowing the application for amendment is affirmed. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court is vacated.

Send down the lower Court's records at once with a copy of the judgment for information and necessary action.

End.
